newsitem.title: CHINA: Star of China's propaganda tsar Ding seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Star of China's propaganda tsar Ding seen rising.

text.p: China's propaganda tsar Ding Guangen will head a new high-level group in charge of ideology for the Communist Party, signalling that the star of the Deng Xiaoping protege is rising, Chinese sources said on Tuesday.

Ding, 67, head of the Propaganda Department of the party's Central Committee, was recently appointed head of the party's Central Leading Group for Construction of Spiritual Civilisation, said sources with close ties to the party who asked not to be identified.

The party has embarked on a crusade to resurrect spiritual civilisation -- party jargon for civic responsibility and socialist ethics -- that officials feel have been eroded by almost two decades of economic reforms.

Most of the party's central leading groups, or policy-making bodies, are headed by members of the Politburo Standing Committee, and Ding's appointment signalled he could join that omnipotent body at the 15th party congress later this year, one source said.

Ding is known to people close to him as "ba ye", or "Eighth Master", in reference to his rank in the party's political hierarchy as the most senior member of the Politburo who does not hold a Standing Committee seat, another source said.
"The Standing Committee has seven members. Ding Guangen is called 'ba ye' because he is the eighth...next in line to join the Standing Committee," the second source said.

The Communist Party is studying a proposal to increase the number of Standing Committee members to nine from seven at the forthcoming party congress, a crucial meeting of the party elite that is held every five years, sources said.

The struggle is already under way in China's secretive party apparatus among its elite for the most coveted top jobs that carry the power to decide China's future direction and policies, and Ding is reported to be a leading player.
The sources dismissed rumours that Ding could be out of a job after the congress after coming under fire for his hardline, conservative stance.
"Do you think he would have been made head of the Leading Group for Construction of Spiritual Civilisation...if he were to step down at the 15th party congress?" the first source said.
The Leading Group for Construction of Spiritual Civilisation is more powerful than the Propaganda Department.
Ding has tightened the party's iron grip on the media in recent years, bringing down the ideological axe on many books, movies and arts events since he took over the propaganda reins in 1992.

A former favoured bridge partner of the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died on February 19, aged 92, Ding is known for his openly hardline approach and last year urged that social science research should stress Marxism and Mao Zedong thought.

Ding is reviled by reform-minded party members, some of whom have accused him of once being a member of the youth league of the Nationalists, the Communists' arch enemy in the 1940s, the sources said.
The Nationalists lost the Chinese civil war to the Communists and fled into exile in Taiwan in 1949. Ding joined the Communist Party in 1956.
